audits.secondSweep: Dedicated P5/P6 sweep done sentence by sentence. Roads and geography: 'the slope fell away', 'The track bent... dropping', 'the track ran east', 'The road went on east', 'the southern track turned... climbing' all use literal topographic verbs, with no fire, intent or cognition verbs. Maps, reports and plans: 'It said stable in three different hands' and 'it says so in three hands' name the real writers (the wardens' hands); the map sentences ('Each was a small neat dot', 'These had roads', 'Thin ruled lines ran up') carry no revision or cognition verb, and the human drawer is named ('Whoever had drawn it', 'somebody had held the sheet down'). Body-part subjects: L13 dying legs (involuntary), L63 palm reach (the palm is the sensing organ), L93 and L205 hand closing (involuntary motif, made explicit by 'without meaning to' at L145 and 'She opened it.' at L205), L265 jaw (noun-phrase fragment in a face catalog) were all kept; L17 'learning from her knees' was killed as a discovery wrapper. Abstract states in body parts: the palm cold (L75, L145, L205, L233) is the literal sensation the chapter is about (subject-matter defense), not an emotion landing. Metaphor chains: the stone-as-lame-horse image (L63 'favouring a leg' to L107 'a limp in it' to L177 'a limp in the hum' to L283 'the whole ring could be limping') is one sustained metaphor in Sylvanas's horsewoman vocabulary. L71 sets it up as her substitute for the magister word she lacks. It is not one subject collecting different human verbs.
